bible_refs.note: Ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν.
ἀγαθὸν ἐπερώτημα ... συνειδήσεως: 1 Peter has συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς ἐπερώτημα εἰς θεόν; Cyril reads ἐκ συνειδήσεως ὀρθῆς ... εἰς Χριστόν.
νεκροῦν τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς = νεκρώσατε οὖν τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ, ὃ δὲ ζῇ, ζῇ τῷ Θεῷ.
τὴν αὐτοῦ νέκρωσιν περιφέροντες ἐν ἰδίοις σώμασιν echoes πάντοτε τὴν νέκρωσιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῷ σώματι περιφέροντες.
συνετάφημεν τῷ Χριστῷ; and the quotation Ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Πατρὸς, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν.
LXX Psalm 23:10 κύριος τῶν δυνάμεων αὐτός ἐστιν; Hebrew/English numbering 24:10.
πάντα γέγονε δι' αὐτοῦ = πάντα δι' αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο.
Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον, καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν.
New lemma: Εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ.
τέθεικεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν = ἐκεῖνος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἔθηκεν (compare John 10:11, 15).

choices.why: σύμφυτοι (literally 'grown together, planted together') is rendered 'united' to match the lemma; Cyril himself explains it as σύμμορφοι and ταυτοειδεῖς.
νοητῶς rendered 'spiritually' (in the inward, understood sense, not bodily).
ὁ τῶν δυνάμεων Κύριος rendered 'the Lord of hosts', the usual English for this LXX title.

pass_a_gloss: [...] made (ἐποιήσατο). so the one naming Christ will not be unmindful (ἀμνημονεύσει) of the Father or the Spirit. since, having become man (γενόμενος ἄνθρωπος), Jesus endured (ἀνέτλη) death for the life of all, the blessed Paul necessarily proceeded (κεχώρηκεν) to what is most needful (χρειωδέστατον) for the present mystagogy (μυσταγωγία); for he had to name the one who suffered (τὸν πεπονθότα). therefore he says: as many as were baptized (ἐβαπτίσθημεν) into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death. for having laid down beforehand (προκαταθέμενοι) as it were the good pledge/appeal (ἐπερώτημα) from right conscience (συνειδήσεως ὀρθῆς) toward Christ, and having received by faith that he died for us and was buried (ἐτάφη) and lived again (ἀνεβίω), we have had the forgiveness (ἄφεσις) of sins through holy baptism, enduring the deadening (νέκρωσις) of sin, and as it were dying with (συναποθνήσκοντες) the one who died for us through deadening (νεκροῦν) the members on earth. for Christ died to sin once for all (ἐφάπαξ), what he lives he lives to God; we endure a death equal (ἴσον) to his and all but are buried with (συντεθάμμεθα), carrying about (περιφέροντες) his deadening in our own bodies; we were buried with (συνετάφημεν) Christ. what we gain (ἀποκερδαίνοντες) he himself will make clear (σαφηνιεῖ): that as Christ was raised (ἠγέρθη) from the dead through the glory (δόξα) of the Father, so we too might walk in newness (καινότητι) of life. for we, as buried with, must also rise with (συνανίστασθαι) intelligibly/spiritually (νοητῶς). if being buried with Christ is to have died to sin, clear that rising with is understood as nothing other than living in righteousness (δικαιοσύνη). he affirms (διαβεβαιοῦται) Christ raised through the Father's glory, not as lacking strength (ἰσχύος ἐπιδεᾶ), for he himself is the Lord of powers (ὁ τῶν δυνάμεων Κύριος); but because it is custom (ἔθος) for Christ and his own to attach (προσάπτειν) things above human nature to the glory of the highest nature. so even if God and Father is said to accomplish (κατορθοῦν) something, not [... text defective: ἐξ οἰκείου μὲν ...] of his activity (ἐνέργεια) over all the Son. for if all things came to be through him, how would anyone doubt (ἐνδοιάσειεν) that he worked (ἐνήργηκε) through the Son also the resurrection of the holy body itself? the Son showing himself active (ἐνεργόν) said to the Jews: destroy (λύσατε) this temple (ναός) and in three days I will raise (ἐγερῶ) it. see how he himself promises to raise his own temple, though the God and Father is said to raise it; for since he himself is the life-making power (ζωοποιὸς δύναμις) of God and Father, he made alive (ἐζωοποίει) his own temple. [lemma] for if we have become grown-together (σύμφυτοι) in the likeness (ὁμοίωμα) of his death etc. the divine Paul says those buried with Christ must expect also to rise with him; 'grown-together' would hint (ὑπεμφήνειεν) intelligibly as it were 'co-formed' (σύμμορφοι) and 'same-formed' (ταυτοειδεῖς). but this must be looked into (περιαθρεῖν): Emmanuel laid down (τέθεικεν) his own soul/life (ψυχή) for us and died according to flesh (κατὰ σάρκα); in what manner were we the baptized buried with him? as having endured with him the death of the flesh? not at all (οὐμενοῦν). how then have we become grown-together in the likeness of his death, come, come, let us say: he died [continues u03-rem-early]
pass_b_english: …has made [a declaration of the whole]. So the one who names Christ will not leave the Father or the Spirit unremembered. But since Jesus, having become man, endured death for the life of all, the blessed Paul had to go on to what was most needful for the sacred teaching at hand, for he had to name the one who suffered. That is why he says, “All of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death” (Romans 6:3).

For having first given, as it were, the good pledge of an upright conscience toward Christ (1 Peter 3:21), and having accepted by faith that he died for us, was buried, and came to life again, we have received the forgiveness of sins through holy baptism. We undergo the deadening of sin, and as it were die together with him who died for us, by putting to death our members that are on the earth (Colossians 3:5). For Christ “died to sin once for all, but the life he lives, he lives to God” (Romans 6:10). We undergo a death equal to his and are all but buried with him, carrying about his dying in our own bodies (2 Corinthians 4:10); and we were buried with Christ (Romans 6:4). What we gain from this he will make clear himself, saying, “so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life” (Romans 6:4). For since we have been buried with him, we must also rise with him spiritually. And if being buried with Christ is having died to sin, then surely it is clear that rising with him can rightly be understood as nothing other than living in righteousness.

He affirms, indeed, that Christ was raised through the glory of the Father, not as though Christ lacked strength, for he himself is the Lord of hosts (Psalm 24:10), but because it is the custom of Christ himself and of his own to ascribe what is beyond human nature to the glory of the supreme nature. So even if God the Father is said to accomplish something, he does not shut the Son out of his activity over all things. For if all things came into being through him (John 1:3), how could anyone doubt that he worked through the Son the resurrection of that holy body as well? Indeed the Son, showing himself active in this, said to the Jews, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up” (John 2:19). See, then, how he promises to raise his own temple himself, although God the Father is said to have raised it. For since he is himself the life-giving power of God the Father, he gave life to his own temple.

“For if we have been united with the likeness of his death,” and so on (Romans 6:5). The inspired Paul says that those who have been buried with Christ ought also to expect to rise with him. The word “united” would suggest, in a spiritual sense, something like “conformed” and “of the same form.” But this point must be examined closely. Emmanuel laid down his own life for us (1 John 3:16) and died according to the flesh. In what way, then, have we who are baptized been buried with him? Was it by enduring with him the death of the flesh? Not at all. How, then, have we been united with the likeness of his death? Come, then, let us say it. He died…
source_text:
ἐποιήσατο. οὐκοῦν ὁ Χριστὸν ὀνομάσας οὐκ ἀμνημονεύσει τοῦ Πατρὸς ἢ τοῦ
Πνεύματος. ἐπειδὴ δὲ γενόμενος ἄνθρωπος, τὸν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἁπάντων ζωῆς ἀνέτλη
θάνατον ὁ Ἰησοῦς, κεχώρηκεν ἀναγκαίως ὁ μακάριος Παῦλος ἐπὶ τὸ ὅτι μάλιστα τῇ
προκειμένῃ μυσταγωγίᾳ χρειωδέστατον· ἔδει γὰρ ὀνομάσαι τὸν πεπονθότα· ταύτῃτοί
φησιν Ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθημεν.
προκαταθέμενοι γὰρ ὥσπερ τὸ ἐκ συνειδήσεως ὀρθῆς ἀγαθὸν ἐπερώτημα εἰς Χριστὸν,
καὶ πίστει παραδεξάμενοι ὅτι καὶ ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν καὶ ἐτάφη καὶ ἀνεβίω, τὴν
ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἐσχήκαμεν διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος, καὶ τὴν τῆς ἁμαρτίας
ὑπομένοντες νέκρωσιν, καὶ οἷον τῷ δι' ἡμᾶς τεθνεῶτι συναποθνήσκοντες διὰ τὸ
νεκροῦν τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. ὁ μὲν γὰρ Χριστὸς "τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ "ἀπέθανεν ἐφάπαξ, ὃ δὲ
ζῇ, ζῇ τῷ Θεῷ·" ἡμεῖς δὲ τὸν ἴσον αὐτῷ θάνατον ὑπομένομεν, καὶ μονονουχὶ
συντεθάμμεθα, τὴν αὐτοῦ νέκρωσιν περιφέροντες ἐν ἰδίοις σώμασιν, συνετάφημεν δὲ
τῷ Χριστῷ. τί δὴ ἄρα ἐντεῦθεν ἀποκερδαίνοντες, σαφηνιεῖ λέγων αὐτός Ἵνα ὥσπερ
ἠγέρθη Χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Πατρὸς, οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι
ζωῆς περιπατήσωμεν· δεῖ γὰρ ἡμᾶς ὡς συντεθαμμένους καὶ συνανίστασθαι νοητῶς· καὶ
εἴπερ ἐστὶ τεθνάναι τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ τὸ συνθάπτεσθαι τῷ Χριστῷ, δῆλον ἂν εἴη δήπουθεν ὡς
οὐχ ἕτερόν τι τὸ συνανίστασθαι νοοῖτ' ἂν εἰκότως, πλὴν ὅτι τὸ ζῆν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ.
Ἐγηγέρθαι μὴν διαβεβαιοῦται Χριστὸν διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ Πατρὸς, οὐχ ὡς ἰσχύος ἐπιδεᾶ·
καὶ γάρ ἐστιν αὐτὸς ὁ τῶν δυνάμεων Κύριος· ἀλλ' ὅτι τὰ ὑπὲρ ἀνθρώπου φύσιν τῇ τῆς
ἀνωτάτω φύσεως δόξῃ προσάπτειν ἔθος αὐτῷ τε Χριστῷ καὶ τοῖς αὐτοῦ. οὐκοῦν κἂν εἴ
τι λέγοιτο κατορθοῦν ὁ Θεὸς 190 καὶ Πατὴρ, οὐκ ἐξ οἰκείου μὲν τῆς ἐφ' ἅπασιν
ἐνεργείας αὐτοῦ τὸν Υἱόν· εἰ γὰρ πάντα γέγονε δι' αὐτοῦ, πῶς ἂν ἐνδοιάσειέν τις ὡς
ἐνήργηκε διὰ Υἱοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἁγίου σώματος τὴν ἀνάστασιν; καὶ γοῦν ὁ Υἱὸς
ἐνεργὸν εἰς τοῦτο δεικνὺς ἑαυτὸν, τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἔφασκε "Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν "τοῦτον,
καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν." ἄθρει δὴ οὖν ὅπως αὐτὸς ἐγείρειν ἐπαγγέλλεται
τὸν ἴδιον ναὸν, καίτοι τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς ἀναστῆσαι λεγομένου· ἐπειδὴ γάρ ἐστιν
αὐτὸς ἡ ζωοποιὸς δύναμις τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς, τὸν ἴδιον ἐζωοποίει ναόν. Εἰ γὰρ
σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ κ.τ.λ. Χρῆναί φησιν ὁ θεσπέσιος
Παῦλος τοὺς συντεθαμμένους Χριστῷ καὶ συναναστήσεσθαι προσδοκᾶν· καὶ τὸ μὲν
σύμφυτοι, τὸ οἱονεὶ σύμμορφοί τε καὶ ταυτοειδεῖς νοητῶς ὑπεμφήνειεν ἄν. πλὴν ἐκεῖνο
περιαθρεῖν ἀναγκαῖον· τέθεικεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν ὁ Ἐμμανουὴλ καὶ
ἀπέθανε κατὰ σάρκα· συντεθάμμεθα δὲ αὐτῷ τίνα δὴ τρόπον ἡμεῖς οἱ βεβαπτισμένοι;
ἆρα ὡς ἀνατλάντες σὺν αὐτῷ τὸν τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατον; οὐμενοῦν. πῶς οὖν ἄρα
σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, φέρε δὴ φέρε λέγωμεν· ἀπέθανε
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Staged new translation checked clause by clause: complete and faithful; citations correct (Romans 6:3, 6:4, 6:5, 6:10; 1 Peter 3:21; Colossians 3:5; 2 Corinthians 4:10; Psalm 24:10 = LXX 23:10; John 1:3; John 2:19; 1 John 3:16). Three fixes in the staging file: (1) τὸν ἴσον αὐτῷ θάνατον is 'a death equal to his', not 'like his'; (2) the damaged clause οὐκ ἐξ οἰκείου μὲν ... τὸν Υἱόν most likely stands for οὐκ ἐξοικίζει ('does not shut out'), so the bracketed '[set] the Son outside' becomes plain 'shut the Son out of' and the translator note was updated (still check the printed PG 74 page); (3) 'united with him in the likeness' added 'with him', which is not in σύμφυτοι ... τῷ ὁμοιώματι, so both the lemma and Cyril's question now read 'united with the likeness of his death'. The u03-rem-early staged row (not in this review set) still uses 'united with him' and should be aligned by its reviewer.

Opens with ἐποιήσατο, the main verb of the sentence that ends u02-rem-close (κἂν εἰ ἕν τις ὀνομάσῃ, δυνάμει θεωρημάτων τὴν τοῦ παντὸς δήλωσιν). The bracketed words '[a declaration of the whole]' repeat that object only so the fragment reads; they add nothing new.
Ends mid-sentence at ἀπέθανε; u03-rem-early continues μὲν γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα Χριστός. The closing ellipsis marks the break.

οὐκ ἐξ οἰκείου μὲν τῆς ἐφ' ἅπασιν ἐνεργείας αὐτοῦ τὸν Υἱόν: the clause has no verb and looks damaged in the copy-text (most likely a misreading of οὐκ ἐξοικίζει, 'does not shut out'). Rendered by that reading and the evident sense: the Father does not shut the Son out of his activity over all things.
ὅτι καὶ ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν καὶ ἐτάφη καὶ ἀνεβίω: possible echo of the creed-like 1 Corinthians 15:3-4, but the wording differs (ἀνεβίω, not ἐγήγερται); left uncited as uncertain.
σύμφυτοι (literally 'grown together, planted together') is rendered 'united' to match the lemma; Cyril himself explains it as σύμμορφοι and ταυτοειδεῖς.
νοητῶς rendered 'spiritually' (in the inward, understood sense, not bodily).
ὁ τῶν δυνάμεων Κύριος rendered 'the Lord of hosts', the usual English for this LXX title.
PG column number 190 and stray quotation marks inside the Scripture quotations in the copy-text are dropped from the reading text.
